verdict.rationale: OpenCode's own GitHub integration provides a trigger-based autonomous workflow. A `/opencode` or `/oc` comment runs it in a GitHub Actions runner, and it fixes issues on a new branch and submits a PR; `--auto` approves permissions for unattended runs. The evidence covers only comment-triggered, one-off runs, with no documented recurring schedules or always-on maintenance agents. The headless `serve` mode is a building block, not a scheduler. Missing for 10: documented scheduled/recurring agent runs, other event triggers (e.g., CI failures, new issues), always-on background maintenance agents, independent hands-on corroboration of autonomous fix workflows.

support.subject: As an ai-native user, I can set up always-on agents that run on schedules or triggers to maintain and fix my software autonomously

citations.quote: Mention `/opencode` or `/oc` in your comment, and OpenCode will execute tasks within your GitHub Actions runner.
Ask OpenCode to fix an issue or implement a feature. And it will work in a new branch and submits a PR with all the changes.
Start OpenCode with `--auto` to automatically approve permission requests that are not explicitly denied.
